title: Spatially resolved single-cell atlas reveals the macroevolutionary trajectory of animal hearts.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Download page lists 13 spatial and 18 single-cell .h5ad files (CNGB FTP STDS0000406, open, no login). HEAD on the merged sc_fordatabase.h5ad gave 6.39 GB. Downloaded and opened 3 files: octopus sc (8,531 cells x 19,308 genes, 6 cell types, 2 batches 'bmk'/'huada'), fly sc (10,291 x 17,985, 11 types incl. 'mt' and 'germline cell'), Ciona spatial (11,620 bins x 18,603 genes, 5 types, x/y coordinates). X holds raw integer counts; obs has 'celltype' and 'subtype' columns plus Seurat cluster columns. Gene IDs are species-specific (Afa000010, KY21 models, FlyBase symbols); no orthology table or protein sequences in the files. GitHub repo ouclian/EvoHeart has analysis scripts only (OrthoFinder, SAMap, SATURN runs), no data tables.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 27 species total (abstract); the download offers single-cell files for 16 species (octopus split in two) and spatial for 13, so ~11 species are presumably genome/bulk only. Total cell count unverified (merged file is 6.39 GB, not downloaded). Annotation method (marker genes on clusters) inferred from obs columns and scripts; no full text was available.

a1_downloadable.note: Open FTP links on CNGB STOmicsDB; three files fetched without login.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked in files: 'celltype' and 'subtype' are columns in obs of every file opened.

a3_inputs_present.note: Raw count matrices present. But cross-species work needs orthology or protein sequences, which are not in the files and must be rebuilt from each species' genome annotation (some custom, e.g. Afa IDs).

a4_units_stated.note: X is raw integer UMI (unique molecular identifier) counts, seen in files; units are implicit but standard for scRNA-seq.

a5_enough_rows.note: 8,531 to 11,620 cells per file opened; total across species not counted. Independent units are only ~16 species, 1-2 samples each.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~1.9 GB for all per-species sc files; merged file 6.39 GB not needed
a6_fits_laptop.note: Per-species files are 20-260 MB each; a sparse load of all fits in 16 GB RAM.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Species count 27 vs 16 single-cell species on download is explainable (not all species have sc data) but not confirmed against the full text.

a8_label_provenance.note: Borderline: cell types are author annotations of clusters computed from the same expression matrix, not an independent measurement. Within-species prediction is circular; only cross-species transfer is a meaningful test.

B1.why: One .h5ad per species; consistent obs schema across the three files opened, but genes don't align across species.

B2.why: All three files opened with h5py at first try; standard AnnData layout.

B3.why: Type names vary per species ('Immnue cell' typo, 'Ventricular Cardiomyocyte', 'mt'); need harmonising, seen in files.

B5.why: Doublet columns show only 'Singlet'; cells already filtered (seen in files).

B6.why: Instruction PDF exists (not opened); many unexplained columns like 'test' and 'type'.

C1.why: Transfer-vs-phylogenetic-distance curve is informative either way, but labels are annotation-derived and authors already ran this.

C2.why: SAMap and SATURN open, already run on this data by the authors; a 2025 NAR benchmark covers cross-phylum transfer.

C3.why: Weak diversity angle: mollusc, arthropod, tunicate hearts are rare in single-cell atlases.

C4.why: Manual cluster annotation in a new species is slow but not costly lab work.

C5.why: SAMap/SATURN runnable as baselines; no published transfer accuracy seen (no full text).

D1.why: ESM-2 protein embeddings (SATURN-style) or TranscriptFormer/UCE, open weights.

D2.why: ESM-2 gene embeddings cache on CPU, but proteomes for ~16 species must first be assembled.

D3.why: ESM-2 MIT licence; CNGB data terms open (not read in detail).

E2.why: 16 single-cell species on the download page.

E4.why: No independent re-annotation; batch pairs exist (bmk/huada) but no label replicate.

E5.why: Cardiomyocytes should transfer via conserved sarcomere genes (myosin, troponin), a textbook signal.

E6.why: Label shuffle and gene-embedding shuffle are runnable.

E7.why: Human Heart Cell Atlas and Tabula Muris hearts give independent annotated data for vertebrates.

E8.why: No full text seen, so no published number to reproduce.

G1.why: Species-specific gene IDs; only fly/human/mouse map directly to standard IDs.

G2.why: Heart Cell Atlas (human), CELLxGENE heart data; join via orthologs only.

G3.why: Ortholog mapping is many-to-many for distant species.

G4.why: Combined question (do human heart cell types transfer to molluscs?) is modestly bigger.

H1.why: Classification across all cell types present; no 'negative' concept, but non-cardiac contaminants included.

H2.why: Chordates, arthropods, molluscs in one consistent protocol.

H3.why: Claim is about reproducing one lab's annotations, not ground-truth identity.

H4.why: Annotation subjectivity not documented in the files.

I1.why: Evo-devo and comparative single-cell community; vague.

I2.why: Could speed annotation of new species' hearts, marginally.

I3.why: Per-type accuracy roughly matches annotation use.

I4.why: Marker-ortholog lookup may do nearly as well for major types.

J1.why: Transfer learning, protein embeddings, grouped evaluation.

J2.why: Cell-type markers are checkable but invertebrate biology is unfamiliar.

J3.why: Transfer-by-distance curve is shareable even if weak.

existing_models.name: SATURN (protein-embedding cross-species integration, Nature Methods 2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: 85.8% median label-transfer accuracy zebrafish to frog, held-out species; authors of this paper ran it on these hearts (run_saturn.v1.0.sh).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved in full; performance declines with phylogenetic distance per the NAR benchmark.

existing_models.name: SAMap (homology-graph cross-species mapping)
existing_models.score_and_split: Outperformed by SATURN by 119% on zebrafish-to-frog per SATURN paper; used by these authors (run_samap.v1.0.py).

existing_models.name: Cross-species integration benchmark (NAR 2025, gkae1316)
existing_models.score_and_split: SAMap and SATURN best for cross-phylum; performance drops ~11-12% with one-to-one orthologs only.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Accuracy declines as phylogenetic distance grows.

existing_models.name: TranscriptFormer (cross-species generative single-cell model, 12 species, 112M cells)

backbone.name: ESM-2 protein language model gene embeddings (SATURN-style); alternatively TranscriptFormer
backbone.hardware: CPU laptop for ESM-2 small checkpoints over ~16 proteomes (~300k proteins, slow); TranscriptFormer inference likely GPU
backbone.licence: ESM-2 MIT; TranscriptFormer licence not checked

integration.partner_dataset: Human Heart Cell Atlas / CELLxGENE heart datasets
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: How far across the animal tree do vertebrate heart cell-type definitions transfer before they stop matching anything?

controls.positive_control: Cardiomyocytes recovered via conserved sarcomere genes; human-to-mouse transfer near-perfect.
controls.external_validation: Human Heart Cell Atlas annotations for the human/mouse end.

honest_claim_h3: Predicts which of one lab's cluster-based heart cell-type labels a cell in an unseen species would receive, from one or two hearts per species.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use gene activity in single heart cells from many animals to predict the cell's type in a species the model never saw.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-cell gene count profiles from ~16 animal species' hearts, about 8,500-11,600 cells per species in the files checked; total unknown.
plain_idea.predict: The cell type (cardiomyocyte, fibroblast, endothelial, immune, neural...), whose true answer is the authors' manual annotation of expression clusters.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Shows how far heart cell identities can be carried across distant animals, helping labs annotating new species; already partly done by the authors with SAMap/SATURN.

more_or_better_data.why: Unusual heart coverage of molluscs, fly, tunicate and lamprey, but SATURN/TranscriptFormer were trained on far more cells; ~16 species here.

confidence_score.why: One annotation per cell and 1-2 samples per species; no replicate labels to calibrate against.

models_beatable.why: SATURN (2024) and SAMap are open, evaluated on held-out species, and were already applied to this exact data by the authors.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No joinable new data measures the same labels the same way; external atlases use different annotation schemes.

label_elsewhere.sources: Human Heart Cell Atlas, CELLxGENE heart datasets, Tabula Muris (known resources); none for invertebrate hearts.
label_elsewhere.why: Vertebrate heart annotations allow external checking at one end of the tree only.

ambitious.why: Publishes cross-species single-cell methods; would need a clear distance-decay result beating SATURN for invertebrates.

realistic.why: Benchmark note on cross-phylum transfer of heart cell types using this atlas.

fallback.why: A negative transfer curve is still a shareable benchmark.

pitch.headline: Open, consistently processed heart single-cell data from ~16 species spanning molluscs, fly, tunicate and vertebrates, downloadable as per-species files.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Octopus, snail, scallop, fly and Ciona hearts in one protocol; files of 20-260 MB each with raw counts and cell-type columns (verified on 3 files).
pitch.the_win: A transfer-accuracy versus divergence-time curve for heart cell types across ~600 million years, compared with SATURN on held-out species.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: We learn where along the tree vertebrate heart cell-type labels stop transferring, which mostly restates the authors' own SAMap/SATURN analysis.
pitch.who_wants_it: Comparative single-cell and evo-devo labs annotating non-model animal hearts; would change how much they trust automatic label transfer.

ml_idea: Leave-one-species-out cell-type transfer using ESM-2 gene embeddings (SATURN-style) versus ortholog-marker baselines, plotting accuracy against divergence time.

effort.compute_note: Estimated only: ~300k proteins across 16 proteomes with ESM-2 small on CPU; per-species files load sparse. Proteomes must be sourced per species.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Confirm protein FASTA files exist publicly for the custom-annotated species (e.g. Achatina 'Afa' gene IDs, Amphioctopus); if not, cross-species embedding is impossible.

verdict_reason: Data is open and clean per species, but labels are cluster annotations and the authors already ran SAMap/SATURN on it; crowded field with no clear edge, and gene IDs need proteomes rebuilt.
